name: AutoNotes
description: AutoNotes is the most affordable AI therapy scribe, starting at $24/month (annual) with unlimited notes on the Pro plan. Built exclusively for mental health professionals, AutoNotes generates SOAP, DAP, BIRP, GIRP, PIE notes plus treatment plans and intake assessments. The platform uses typed prompts and checkbox-based input rather than ambient recording, making it best for post-session documentation. With 80,000+ clinicians, AutoNotes has grown rapidly on price positioning—but it lacks native EHR integration (copy-paste or Chrome extension only) and doesn't offer real-time ambient AI like Mentalyc or Upheal. Therapists who want the cheapest option accept the workflow tradeoffs.

faqs.q: How much does AutoNotes cost in 2026?
faqs.a: AutoNotes Economy costs $24/month (annual) or $29/month (monthly) for 30 notes. Pro costs $49/month (annual) for unlimited notes. Team plans run $39/provider/month (minimum 3). This makes AutoNotes the most affordable mental health AI scribe on the market.

No. AutoNotes uses typed prompts and checkbox-based input, not real-time ambient recording. You complete documentation after sessions by typing session recaps or uploading audio. If you want live ambient AI, use Mentalyc or Upheal instead.
Yes. AutoNotes is HIPAA compliant and now provides a BAA for all customers using PHI. This is an update from older policies—the platform now explicitly permits PHI per the AutoNotes Trust Center.

faqs.q: AutoNotes vs Mentalyc: which is better?
faqs.a: Choose AutoNotes if price is your top priority ($24/mo vs Mentalyc's $20-70/mo). Choose Mentalyc if you want ambient session recording, modality-aware notes (CBT, DBT), and Alliance Genie therapeutic tracking. AutoNotes uses post-session typed input; Mentalyc records live.

faqs.q: Does AutoNotes integrate with my EHR?
faqs.a: AutoNotes uses copy-paste or a Chrome extension to insert notes into SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, and TheraNest. There is no native API integration that auto-populates fields. Manual insertion adds overhead as caseloads grow.
